claim:
Let \(X=(\mathbb R^2,N)\) with
\[
N(u,v)=\max\{|u|,|v|,|u-v|\},
\]
the affine-regular hexagonal norm. For Birkhoff--James orthogonality \(x\perp_B y\), set
\[
J_\perp(X)=\sup_{\substack{x,y\in S_X\\x\perp_B y}}
\min\{N(x-y),N(x+y)\},
\qquad
g_\perp(X)=\inf_{\substack{x,y\in S_X\\x\perp_B y}}
\max\{N(x-y),N(x+y)\}.
\]
Then
\[
J_\perp(X)=g_\perp(X)=\frac32.
\]
More strongly, for every unit Birkhoff pair \(x\perp_B y\), the following are equivalent:
\[
\min\{N(x-y),N(x+y)\}=\frac32,
\]
\[
\max\{N(x-y),N(x+y)\}=\frac32,
\]
and, up to a linear isometry of \(X\), replacing \(y\) by \(-y\), and reversing the ordered pair,
\[
(x,y)=\left((1,0),\left(\frac12,1\right)\right).
\]
Hence every extremizer of either orthogonal constant is automatically isosceles,
\[
N(x-y)=N(x+y)=\frac32,
\]
and all extremizers form one symmetry orbit.

correctness.rationale: The unit sphere is exhausted by open edges and vertices under the linear isometries \(R(u,v)=(u-v,u)\) and \(S(u,v)=(v,u)\). On an open edge \(x=(1,t)\), Birkhoff orthogonality forces \(y=(0,\pm1)\), giving chord lengths \(1+t\) and \(2-t\). At a vertex \(x=(1,0)\), the complete norming-functional segment \(f_a(u,v)=u-av\) forces \(y=\pm(a,1)\), giving \(1+a\) and \(2-a\). In both strata, equality for either the James-side upper bound or the Schäffer-side lower bound occurs only at parameter \(1/2\), where both chord lengths equal \(3/2\). The symmetry generators identify the two equality representatives after order reversal.
risks: The proof is specific to the real two-dimensional affine-regular hexagon.
The classification is modulo the stated norm isometries, sign reversal of the second vector, and order reversal.

value.rationale: The affine-regular hexagon is a canonical Radon plane in which Birkhoff orthogonality has unusually strong symmetry, and the 2022 paper uses it as a basic test case for the newly introduced orthogonal James and Schäffer constants. A complete equality classification is therefore a natural structural refinement of the known values, not an arbitrary parameter slice. The result shows that both a supremum and an infimum are rigid at exactly the same Birkhoff pair orbit and forces the extremal pair to be isosceles. Later work again singles out affine-regular hexagons as extremal for broader Birkhoff-orthogonal constants, increasing the utility of an exact pair-level benchmark.
risks: The theorem refines one canonical example rather than establishing a family-wide rigidity principle.
